settings.label: Web API key
settings.meaning: Identifies the Firebase project to the Identity Toolkit API, for sign-in, token refresh and password resets. Not a secret: Firebase says it's OK to include in code.
settings.whereToFind: Firebase console › Settings › General › Your apps › your web app › Config: apiKey. Test and production are separate Firebase projects, each with its own key; the keys look alike, so nothing tells one from the other.

settings.label: Auth domain
settings.meaning: The domain the browser's Firebase SDK signs in through (Google and GitHub sign-in). The server doesn't call it; it's here so the app can hand the browser its config.
settings.whereToFind: Firebase console › Settings › General › Your apps › your web app › Config: authDomain, usually <projectId>.firebaseapp.com.

settings.label: Project ID
settings.meaning: The Firebase project whose ID tokens the app accepts: every token's aud must be it, and its iss https://securetoken.google.com/<projectId>.
settings.whereToFind: Firebase console › Settings › General: Project ID. Use a separate Firebase project for test.

settings.label: Service account key
settings.meaning: The project's service account key file, as JSON. It signs the requests that manage users (look up, create, delete, set a password, revoke sessions) and the revocation check. Leave it unset if the app only verifies tokens and signs users in.
settings.whereToFind: Firebase console › Settings › Service accounts › Generate new private key. The whole downloaded file is the value. It must belong to the same project as the project ID.

operations.name: keys.get
operations.purpose: Reads the public keys Firebase signs ID tokens with (RS256), at https://www.googleapis.com/service_accounts/v1/jwk/securetoken@system.gserviceaccount.com, kept for the Cache-Control max-age of the answer.

operations.name: accounts.signInWithPassword
operations.purpose: Signs a user in with email and password, with the web API key: an ID token, a refresh token, or an MFA challenge.

operations.name: accounts.signUp
operations.purpose: Creates an email and password user, with the web API key (self sign-up; the email is unverified).

operations.name: accounts.sendOobCode
operations.purpose: Has Firebase email a password reset (PASSWORD_RESET) or a sign-in link (EMAIL_SIGNIN), with the web API key.

operations.name: accounts.resetPassword
operations.purpose: Sets a new password with the oobCode from a password reset email, with the web API key.

operations.name: accounts.signInWithEmailLink
operations.purpose: Signs a user in with the email and the oobCode from a sign-in link, creating the user when none has the email, with the web API key.

operations.name: token.refresh
operations.purpose: Exchanges a refresh token for a new ID token, at https://securetoken.googleapis.com/v1/token, with the web API key.

operations.name: serviceAccount.token
operations.purpose: Exchanges a JWT signed with the service account's key (RS256, scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/identitytoolkit) for a Google OAuth access token, at https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token. The token is reused until shortly before it expires.

operations.name: projects.accounts.lookup
operations.purpose: Reads users by id or by email, with the service account.

operations.name: projects.accounts.signUp
operations.purpose: Creates a user, with the service account: the email can be marked verified.

operations.name: projects.accounts.update
operations.purpose: Sets a user's password, or revokes every refresh token issued to them before now (validSince), with the service account.

operations.name: projects.accounts.delete
operations.purpose: Deletes a user, with the service account.

operations.name: projects.accounts.sendOobCode
operations.purpose: Makes a password reset or sign-in link without emailing it (returnOobLink), so the app sends it, with the service account.
